book.title: The AI Ready School
book.author: Stephen R. Jordan
book.volume: Volume X of The Operating Discipline for AI Library

name: AI in Education
blurb: Artificial intelligence is already in schools, in the tools teachers plan with, the software students practise on, and the systems that run buses and budgets. These pages, built on the book The AI Ready School, set out what works from preschool to graduation, what the evidence shows, and the rule that runs through all of it: AI may inform a decision about a child, but a named person makes it.
title: AI in Education
answer: Artificial intelligence is already in schools, in the tools teachers plan with, the software students practise on, and the systems that run buses and budgets. These pages, built on the book The AI Ready School, set out what works from preschool to graduation, what the evidence shows, and the rule that runs through all of it: AI may inform a decision about a child, but a named person makes it.

children.name: Getting Oriented
children.blurb: The first four chapters lay the foundation for everything that follows. They explain what AI can and cannot do, the ten patterns that account for nearly every idea in the Volume, the laws and rules that protect students, and a simple method for piloting and measuring any new tool.

children.name: The Classroom
children.blurb: Part II, The Classroom, covers AI in each stage and subject. It begins with preschool through second grade, then turns to reading and writing, mathematics, science and computing, social studies and world languages, the arts and physical education, and personalized learning and tutoring.

children.name: Every Student, Every Family
children.blurb: Part III, Every Student, Every Family, covers special education and accessibility, English learners and newcomers, communication with families, wellbeing and safety, and counseling and college. These chapters address the students and families who most need careful attention.

children.name: Running the School
children.blurb: Part IV, Running the School, covers teacher planning and grading, assessment and data, operations and finance, and people and leadership. These chapters speak most directly to principals, district leaders, and board members.

sections.body: This part of the Volume covers the whole of school life where AI now shows up, from the classroom to the business office, and it treats schools as different from businesses because a school is also responsible for how AI affects children's learning and for protecting them while it happens. The book describes AI arriving faster than almost any technology before it, with students finding free chat tools before districts had policies and teachers using AI to plan lessons before anyone trained them. It gathers 300 practical ideas across 20 chapters, from preschool through graduation, and labels each one by the strength of its evidence. The central example is the same kind of tool producing opposite results in two places, which is why the book says the outcome depends on choices adults make rather than on the technology itself.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The book finds that AI tutoring works when teachers design the opening prompt and stay in the room, and harms learning when students use plain chatbots on their own and copy answers. It finds that weekly messages to families about missed work, grades, and absences cut course failures, that plain supportive notices beat legal language, and that personal reminders from a student's own counselor helped students reach college while national campaigns did nothing. It is direct about what does not work: AI detectors misclassify writing by students still learning English and a detection score must never be treated as proof, no evidence shows online monitoring prevents harm, and no independent evaluation of AI security systems in schools was found. The rule it holds to is that people make every decision affecting a student, names and details stay out of any tool without a signed data privacy agreement, learning tools give hints rather than answers, every AI draft is checked by a person, and every flag leads to a person who reaches out.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages move from orientation to the classroom, then to families, then to running the school. Getting Oriented gives the reader the frame, the evidence labels, the five rules, and the honest account of what is unknown, so a teacher, leader or parent can judge how much weight any later idea can bear. The Classroom holds the practical ideas for planning, teaching, feedback and grading, organized by subject and grade, which is where a teacher would go first. Every Student, Every Family speaks to parents and to the adults who reach out to them, including the questions a parent should be able to ask a school and the answers a good school gives. Running the School carries the policy, pilot, purchasing and professional learning guidance for principals, district leaders and board members, and it is where the argument lands that tools do not change schools and the people in them do.
